html:
SMTO-GML-0022 — SMTO lost its place in a Gmail list

GUID: 39b8fadf-141f-4632-90d3-90dbfc07379a
Slug: gmail-page-token-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO was showing a long Gmail list in pages, such as your labels, filters or emails, and the marker for the next page was no longer valid. Nothing in your mailbox was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to show the list again from the start, for example "list all my Gmail labels again". Starting over gives SMTO a fresh, valid place to continue from.
  2. Ask for the next page soon after, only once, and without switching to a different list or search in between. Each next-page marker works once, only for the list it came from, and expires after about 10 minutes.
  3. If the list is very long, ask SMTO to narrow it, for example only labels whose names start with a certain word. A shorter list needs fewer pages.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the first page of the list and can continue to the next page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A paged Gmail listing received a page_token it cannot use: for OAuth accounts the local labels/filters offset is not a non-negative integer; for app-password accounts read through the Gateway the page handle is unknown, expired (10 minutes), already used, issued for a different listing, or the folder changed.

What this means

  • Local pagination cannot parse page_token as a nonnegative integer offset. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Local pagination cannot parse page_token as a nonnegative integer offset.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish this local offset token from opaque provider pagination tokens.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._page parses page_token as a non-negative decimal offset for list_labels and list_filters; the Gateway IMAP runtime (gmail_runtime cursor store) accepts a one-use handle for 10 minutes and only for the same account, method and arguments, and rejects it if the folder UIDVALIDITY changed. Restart the listing with an empty page_token and pass only the next_page_token returned by that same listing, promptly and once.
  • Restart pagination from the first page and use the new returned token.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh first page and its returned token continue the intended list.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
